title: Eyesight Rules & Medical Conditions
whatItIs: Every driver must meet the standards of vision for driving and tell DVLA about conditions that could affect safe driving. The eyesight check opens every driving test.

keyFacts.text: You MUST be able to read a number plate in good daylight from 20 m (20.5 m for an old-style plate).
If you need glasses or contact lenses to read the plate, you MUST wear them at all times while driving.
You MUST also have visual acuity of at least decimal 0.5 (6/12) on the Snellen scale and an adequate field of vision.
You MUST report to DVLA any health condition likely to affect your driving.
You MUST surrender your licence if your doctor tells you to stop driving for 3 months or more.

keyFacts: Not telling DVLA about a condition: fine of up to £1,000, and prosecution if you have an accident.

items.title: First plate
items.text: Clearly more than 20 m away, in good daylight.

items.title: Second plate
items.text: If misread; the candidate may walk to just over the distance.

items.title: Third plate
items.text: Exact distance measured with the official tape.

items.title: Still misread
items.text: Test ends as a fail. DVLA is told; licence revoked.

a.label: Must tell DVLA (car licence)
points: Eyesight problem affecting both eyes, or the only eye
Notifiable conditions, e.g. epilepsy, sleep apnoea, glaucoma
A condition that has got worse since the licence was issued

b.label: No need to tell DVLA
points: Surgery for short sight, if you meet the standards

onTheTest.question: Your pupil reads the number plate wearing glasses, then takes them off to drive. What should the examiner do?
options: Let them drive, as the eyesight check is passed
Explain the glasses must be worn to drive, or the test ends
Record a serious fault and carry on
Ask them to read a plate at 15 m without glasses
onTheTest.why: DT1 6.17: if the plate can only be read with glasses, the law requires them to be worn whenever driving. Unless they are worn, the test will be terminated.

onTheTest.question: A pupil asks which eyesight issue they do NOT have to report to DVLA. What do you tell them?
options: A problem with their only working eye
onTheTest.why: You must tell DVLA about an eyesight problem affecting both eyes (or the remaining eye). This does not include being short or long sighted or colour blind.

traps: An examiner must never ask a candidate to read a plate at less than 20 metres.
Bioptic (telescope) spectacles are not accepted for driving in Great Britain.
A candidate with reading difficulties can write the number plate down instead of reading it aloud.
From 70, notifiable conditions are declared on the licence renewal form.
